jobs.description:
Job Description

Recognized by Newsweek in 2024 and 2025 as one of America's Greatest Workplaces for Diversity

Make Lives Better Including Your Own. If you want to work in an environment where you can become your best possible self, join us! You’ll earn more than a paycheck; you can find opportunities to grow your career through professional development, as well as ongoing programs catered to your overall health and wellness. Full suite of health insurance, life insurance and retirement plans are available and vary by employment status.

We believe in rewarding those who build our future. This position includes eligibility for equity grants under our long-term incentive plan that vest over time, allowing you to share in the value you help create.

Part And Full Time Benefits Eligibility

Medical, Dental, Vision insurance
401(k)
Associate assistance program
Employee discounts
Referral program
Early access to earned wages for hourly associates (outside of CA)
Optional voluntary benefits including ID theft protection and pet insurance

Full Time Only Benefits Eligibility

Paid Time Off
Paid holidays
Company provided life insurance
Adoption benefit
Disability (short and long term)
Flexible Spending Accounts
Health Savings Account
Optional life and dependent life insurance
Optional voluntary benefits including accident, critical illness and hospital indemnity Insurance, and legal plan
Tuition reimbursement

Base pay in range will be determined by applicant’s skills and experience. Full-time associates in role are eligible for an annual bonus incentive and sales referral bonuses. Temporary associates are not benefits eligible but may participate in the company’s 401(k) program.

Veterans, transitioning active duty military personnel, and military spouses are encouraged to apply. To support our associates in their journey to become a U.S. citizen, Brookdale offers to advance fees for naturalization (Form N-400) application costs, up to $725, less applicable taxes and withholding, for qualified associates who have been with us for at least a year.

The application window is anticipated to close within 30 days of the date of the posting.

Responsibilities

Leads the day-to-day operations of a larger community of 60-65 units and two product lines or 65-175 units with up to two product lines. Is responsible for the community’s associate relations, resident and resident family engagement and connection, financial performance, and regulatory compliance. Creates and executes the business plan and develops the team to become a preferred senior living community in the market, while growing revenue and profitability in partnership with the district team. Works with sales to drive sales results. Creates an inclusive community culture that provides high quality resident experiences and care and engages residents, families, and associates.

Responsible for all operations within the community, interacting with staff and residents, prospects, or their family members or representatives, as necessary.
Develops and implements business plan to become a preferred senior living community in the local market and creates, analyzes, and executes annual operating and capital budgets; manages community performance against goals; sets plans to improve or maintain performance to Company service and financial standards.
Builds and maintains strong working relationships with management team and encourages teamwork and collaboration; cultivates an inclusive community culture. Empowers department leaders to supervise, direct, and motivate staff and to proactively recognize and solve issues. Holds department leaders accountable for department performance. Provides assistance to leaders and staff as needed. Ensures community maintains appropriate staffing levels to meet the needs of residents and in accordance with applicable legal requirements.
Supports department leaders to attract, develop, engage, and retain associates in accordance with Company policies. Responsible for recruiting and hiring high quality and engaged associates and ensuring they are appropriately trained and developed to meet the needs of residents. Reviews promotions, development plans, disciplinary actions, and termination decisions ensuring consistency in the selection and retention of quality associates. Analyzes trends and implements strategies to reduce turnover and increase retention.
Builds high degree of resident satisfaction and retention. Is responsible for maintaining positive resident relations and is accessible and approachable to residents and their families. Is proactive in solving resident problems and resolving issues. Leads effort to leverage satisfied residents and families to grow community occupancy; executes renewal program with existing residents. Partners with Resident Council as necessary. Administers resident satisfaction and other surveys and works with department leaders and district team to create plan to address opportunities for improvement in resident satisfaction, experience, and engagement.
For assisted living or memory care communities, ensures collaborative relationship with community clinical leader to ensure community’s care and services are appropriate to meet the needs of residents. Oversees resident services including the admission process, healthcare management, and maintenance of resident documentation to ensure high quality services and compliance with Company policy and applicable legal requirements. Empowers department leaders to demonstrate the same for their area. Ensures service plan reviews are conducted, consistent with applicable legal requirements, with appropriate clinical care team members and resident families to maintain the personal dignity of residents.
Demonstrates a high degree of financial acumen as it relates to community operations. Analyzes, develops, and executes annual operating and capital budgets; works to meet or exceed budgeted revenue, profitability, and occupancy goals. Proactively creates plans to overcome unanticipated expenses or revenue shortfalls. Continually explores means of revenue enhancement and expense reduction, while meeting the needs of residents and adhering to Company policies and applicable regulations.
Drives sales and marketing efforts in collaboration with the community sales leader to meet or exceed occupancy or revenue targets by developing new business, generating leads, and building strategic relationships. Engages with prospects who tour the community. Identifies trends and works with sales leader to implement approved sales and marketing activities and strategies to maximize revenue (RevPAR).
Identifies and builds positive relationships with local influencers and professionals to raise community profile. Becomes active in social and civic affairs of the local community that align with the Company’s mission. Represents the community and the Company to governmental agencies (as appropriate), professional organizations, community groups, and other appropriate public agencies and groups.
Ensures buildings, grounds, and property are up to Company standards through the oversight of preventative maintenance systems and programs and frequent inspections that meet Company standards of excellence.
Enforces current Company policies and procedures. Maintains applicable licenses in accordance with Company, Federal, State, and local requirements.

This job description represents an overview of the responsibilities for the above referenced position. It is not intended to represent a comprehensive list of responsibilities. An associate should perform all duties as assigned by their supervisor.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor’s Degree required. Minimum of three years related in operational leadership experience required. Additional years of experience can be substituted for the education requirement on a year-for-year basis.

Certifications, Licenses, And Other Special Requirements

Must have a valid administrator license in states where required. Must have a valid driver’s license and access to a private vehicle for business use.

Management/Decision Making

Uses strong analytic skills and an in-depth understanding of the organization and the business in order to handle arising problems and issues. Demonstrates leadership ability to be responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of resident care, marketing, food service, housekeeping, and maintenance units. Carries out supervisory responsibilities, including managing department leaders, in accordance with the Company’s policies and applicable laws.

Knowledge And Skills

Has an advanced knowledge of the organization, industry, and a functional discipline. Extensive understanding of technical areas gained through experience and used to complete and/or oversee assignments. Familiarity with Microsoft software preferred. Excellent written and oral communications skills are essential. Ability to prioritize and effectively manage multiple tasks is essential. Ability to delegate assignments to the appropriate individuals based on their skills, roles, and interests. Success in driving results. jobs.description:
Company Description

The San Francisco Adult Probation Department values the individuality and diversity of justice involved adults, recognize the unique challenges they face, and invest in their success through services designed to help them permanently exit the criminal justice system. Our reentry and rehabilitative services complement our supervision strategies by providing a unique blend of opportunity and accountability. We extend a continuum of integrated services to address our client’s criminogenic needs and empower them to become productive members of the community. SFAPD dedicates endless energy toward enhancing public safety, seeking victim restoration and accountability, providing structured and evidence-based supervision, all on the behalf of the Superior Court of San Francisco.

Job Description

Reporting to the Department Head, Deputy Directors function at the highest level of department management and are responsible for all functions and activities of a major division or area. Positions in this class are exempt from Civil Service appointment (Charter Section 10.104); appointment to Deputy Director positions are made by the department head and appointees serve at their discretion.

Under general direction of the Chief Adult Probation Officer of the Adult Probation Department (ADP), the Deputy Director of Finance and Administrative Services is senior executive -level manager that plans, develops and implements all fiscal and administrative functions and activities of the department.

Positions in this class provide executive direction for highly specialized professional functions within departments. Incumbents in these positions make decisions critically impacting diverse functions of the division/bureau; manage organizational changes; and provide direction to Division Managers responsible for major program areas.

Deputy Directors within a single department may be allocated at different classification levels, including acting on behalf of the Chief Adult Probation Officer

This position oversees the financial, budgetary, procurement, fiscal and administrative affairs of the Adult Probation Department. The incumbent advises the Chief Adult Probation Officer on financial and budgetary issues, operations, human resources planning and administrative policy and legislative matters. The primary functions of this position are as follows:

Department Accounting Manager
Serve as subject matter expert overseeing accounting and budgeting structures and hierarchies, and developing and maintaining related policies and procedures
Provide leadership, coordination, and primary point of contact for internal and external auditors; developing, composing, and implementing corrective action plans, progress reporting, and practice change across the department.
Lead development and implementation of internal controls to ensure fiduciary integrity and compliance with city/county, state, and federal fiscal, accounting, budgeting, contracting and purchasing policies and procedures and regulatory requirements.

Chief Budget Strategist:
Develop and coordinate budget development processes and strategies to maximize funding streams from state, federal, sales, tax, vehicles, and grants.
Develop and manage the department’s master budget production schedule, convening division budget meetings to develop budget recommendations;
Compile and consolidate annual budget recommendations, appropriation modifications and mid-cycle budget amendments, and revenue and expense cost impact analysis;
Oversee position control and reconciliation; and managing budget expenditure and revenue projections, reporting, and budgetary controls.
Plan, develop and present budget narratives, budget policies and procedures, and ensuring budget system integrity and reconciliation, and budget variance reporting.

Procurement
Serve as subject matter expert overseeing all procurement including request for proposal and other solicitation, personal service contract(PSC) development, establishing procurement policies and procedures.

Interpret and ensure compliance with city procurement regulations
Oversee financial integrity and reconciliation of financial, accounting, budgeting, banking, and contracting systems
Develop and producing financial and statistical reporting of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial projections
Account reconciliations, discrepancy resolutions, cashiering and escheatment functions, and adjusting accounting transactions and write-offs.
Plan, develop, and implement financial business analytics and dashboard reporting system solution to integrate financial data in disparate accounting, banking, and case management systems.
Develop and implement financial and statistical feasibility studies for compliance reporting, legislative impact and funding analysis, new operations and program proposals, grant proposals, capital projects and facility renovations and relocations.

Human Resources
Manage and oversee all areas of human resources including leave management, reasonable accommodations, examination development and administration, recruitment, labor and employee relations, payroll and operations.
Manage and coordinate the development and review of departmental personnel policies and procedures.
Interpret and ensure compliance with CSC Rules, City Charter, Collective Bargaining Agreements (CBAs), and other employment laws and regulations.
Oversee the day-to-day responsibilities of the ADA reasonable accommodation and leave management programs as well as Workers’ Compensation claims.
Develop and provide training to managers on employee/labor issues and trends, including administration and facilitation of disciplinary and grievance processes and performance management
Advise managers and supervisors on employee/labor relations issues, CBA interpretation, disciplinary actions, grievances, employee coaching, counseling, performance management, employment laws, CSC rules, City Charter, City and County of San Francisco (CCSF) policies, Department policies.

Compliance
Monitor, analyze, and interpret federal, state and local legislation and regulations;
Conduct full internal affairs investigations
Serve as department audit manager coordinating responses to local, state and federal audits.
Develop and implement strategies and administrative, personnel, financial and operations policies and procedures to achieve compliance;
Develop recommendations to minimize department financial and programmatic impacts.
Consult with department executives, directors, managers and staff to plan and develop new and updated administrative/management policies and procedures.
Consult with department executives, directors, managers and staff to plan, develop, and implement Department’s strategic plans including a Racial Equity, Five-Year Plans, etc.

Supervision
Planning, organizing, and managing day-to-day operations of the Finance and Administrative Services of the Department including subordinate work assignments and work schedules to ensure continuity of services to the general public and clients;
Supervise and train staff, evaluate their performance and takes or recommends appropriate action where disciplinary matters are concerned.

Department Representation
Developing and maintaining collaboratively works with other City departments, Superior Court, and other organizations on joint funding projects including inter-agency agreements, MOUs, grant agreements, contracts, and oversees integrity of financial, accounting, and budgeting operations.
Representing the department for budgeting, accounting, and financial related matters with City and County agencies, state and federal agencies and committees, and other organizations including the Mayor’s Budget Office, Board of Supervisors, other county, state, and federal agencies, and the public.
Developing and maintaining relationships with elected and appointed officials, state and federal representatives, community groups, and labor organizations.

Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Possession of a baccalaureate degree in accounting, finance, business administration, public administration, or a closely related field; AND

Three (3) years of progressively responsible managerial experience directing a complex financial and administrative operation, all of which must include supervisory experience.

Education Substitution:
Additional years of experience as listed above may substitute up to two years of the required degree (on a year for year basis).

Additional Information

The City and County of San Francisco encourages women, minorities and persons with disabilities to apply. Applicants will be considered regardless of their sex, race, age, religion, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition (associated with cancer, a history of cancer, or genetic characteristics), HIV/AIDS status, genetic information, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, military and veteran status, or other protected category under the law.

jobs.description:
About SF New Deal:

SF New Deal (SFND) is a 501(c)3 nonprofit that provides supportive services and financial opportunities for small businesses in San Francisco. Our mission is to strengthen neighborhoods by making it easier for under-resourced small business owners to succeed. We envision and are building towards a vibrant San Francisco with diverse and thriving small businesses.

Our team is growing rapidly to build and deliver innovative and responsive community-centered solutions to some of San Francisco’s most persistent challenges. Since our launch in March 2020, we’ve had significant impact and disbursed over $60 million dollars to over 2000 small businesses citywide through a host of diverse programs. Our work is funded through private donations and government contracts.

We’re a team of collaborative optimists and would love to have you join and build with us.

About the role:

SF New Deal seeks a strategic, collaborative, and execution-oriented Deputy Director of Small Business Systems & Navigation to lead the coordination of the small-business support ecosystem in San Francisco.

San Francisco has a substantial network of public agencies, nonprofit organizations, lenders, funders, technical-assistance providers, and neighborhood-based initiatives serving small businesses. Yet entrepreneurs are often required to navigate multiple applications, overlapping eligibility requirements, and informal referral processes to find the support that meets their needs.

The Deputy Director will lead SF New Deal’s No Wrong Door initiative, a multi-year effort to create a clearer and more coordinated entry point for small-business assistance. The initiative will establish shared referral infrastructure, strengthen coordination among providers, and develop technology that helps businesses identify and access appropriate capital, technical assistance, and other resources.
This is a senior leadership role for someone who can work across strategy, partnerships, program operations, technology, and data. The Deputy Director will serve as the principal architect and accountable driver for the initiative, moving it from stakeholder alignment and prototyping through public launch, adoption, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategy, Systems Design, and Implementation
Define and manage the strategy, operating model, implementation plan, budget, and performance measures for the No Wrong Door initiative.
Design a coordinated intake, assessment, referral, and follow-up system that makes it easier for small businesses to access appropriate capital, technical assistance, and other resources.
Lead the initiative from provider mapping and prototyping through launch, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Oversee the development of accessible, secure, and practical technology supporting intake, eligibility assessment, referrals, and provider coordination.
Manage staff, consultants, vendors, and cross-functional workstreams to deliver the initiative on time and within budget.

Partnerships, Provider Coordination, and Adoption
Build and manage a network of government agencies, community organizations, lenders, funders, technical-assistance providers, and neighborhood partners.
Establish shared referral protocols, service expectations, eligibility information, data-sharing practices, and mechanisms for resolving unsuccessful referrals.
Convene partners to identify service gaps, reduce duplication, and improve coordination across the small-business support ecosystem.
Lead provider onboarding, training, communications, and adoption of the intake and referral system.
Represent SF New Deal with senior external stakeholders, funders, public agencies, and community partners.

Operations, Data, and Continuous Improvement
Oversee the day-to-day operation and quality of the navigation and referral system, including referral integrity, responsiveness, and user experience.
Establish measures for access, referral completion, response time, service utilization, capital connection, equity, and business-owner satisfaction.
Use quantitative data and stakeholder feedback to identify gaps, improve workflows, and inform recommendations to providers, funders, and public agencies.
Produce regular reports for organizational leadership, funders, and participating partners.
Ensure the initiative remains responsive to changing business needs, provider capacity, eligibility requirements, and funding conditions.

Key Proficiencies:

Visionary strategic thinking with a proven ability to design and lead programs that anticipate future needs and opportunities for small businesses.
Strong partnership skills, with the ability to collaborate closely with peers, direct reports and senior leadership, to bring program ideas to life and refine them as needed.
Ability to synthesize complex data and feedback from multiple sources into actionable program strategies that drive impact.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate both internal teams and external stakeholders around a shared vision for the future.
Experience with program evaluation and a data-driven approach to assessing program effectiveness and impact.
Creative problem-solving abilities, with a focus on continuous improvement and innovation in program design.
Strong understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing small businesses, particularly in under-resourced communities.

Qualifications
At least five years of experience in economic development, small-business support, public-sector innovation, nonprofit leadership, community development, financial inclusion, program design, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through implementation.
Strong knowledge of the needs and operating realities of small businesses, particularly businesses owned by historically underserved entrepreneurs.
Track record of building alignment among government agencies, nonprofit organizations, financial institutions, funders, and community partners.
Experience designing or improving intake, referral, navigation, case-management, or service-delivery systems.
Experience managing technology-enabled projects, digital products, databases, customer-relationship-management systems, or similar platforms.
Strong project and people management skills, including experience managing staff, consultants, vendors, budgets, and multiple concurrent workstreams.
Ability to define performance measures, interpret quantitative and qualitative data, and use findings to improve programs and influence strategy.
Excellent facilitation, negotiation, writing, presentation, and relationship-management skills.
Ability to move comfortably between high-level strategy and detailed execution in a fast-changing environment.
Sound judgment, strong follow-through, and a collaborative leadership style.
Commitment to equitable access, user-centered design, and reducing administrative burdens for small-business owners.
Bachelor’s degree in public policy, public administration, business administration, economics, urban planning, information systems, data analytics, community development, or a closely related field; advanced degree preferred.
Experience working in the San Francisco small-business, economic-development, or community-development ecosystem.
Familiarity with small-business lending, grants, technical assistance, commercial leasing, permitting, procurement, or neighborhood economic development.
Experience launching a new program, collaborative network, or technology-enabled service.
Familiarity with data-sharing agreements, privacy considerations, and responsible uses of AI.

Across all platforms, the Deputy Director is expected to always act professionally, use good judgment, and bring a hospitality mindset to programs. In all interactions, they should thoughtfully and empathetically manage expectations with clients, partners, and team members with clarity and consistency.

You’ll also attend 8 in-person team events per year: annual kickoff, midyear, and 6 culture and team-building events.

Another Source’s client, Cal State Long Beach
, is recruiting a Senior Director of Development, College of Health and Human Services (CHHS)

Here’s a little about Cal State Long Beach and the position they are recruiting for:

Cal State Long Beach, one of the largest universities in the CSU system, is located in Long Beach on a beautifully landscaped, 320-acre campus near the ocean and the thriving downtown area. The school’s faculty and staff are engaged in a broad array of high-quality undergraduate and graduate programs, significant research, in addition to a wide range of community and professional service organizations.

About the University Relations and Development Team:

The University Relations and Development (URD) division at CSU Long Beach builds relationships and generates resources that strengthen the university’s capacity to achieve its mission. The development team partners closely with colleges, university leadership, alumni, donors, corporations, and foundations to advance philanthropic support across the institution. Through strategic fundraising, donor engagement, and cross-campus collaboration, the team works to foster a strong culture of philanthropy that supports student success, innovation, and institutional priorities. The team is focused on building meaningful, long-term relationships that deepen alumni and donor connection to the university

To learn more about the University Relations and Development division, please visit: https://www.csulb.edu/university-relations-and-development

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $130,000- 150,000, commensurate with experience.

About the role:

The Senior Director of Development for the College of Health and Human Services (CHHS) is responsible for securing major gifts of $25,000+ with a focus on gifts above $100,000, including principal gifts at the $1 million+ level, in support of the university and CHHS priorities. Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Development, this role serves as the college’s primary development officer and partners closely with the dean, faculty, and university leadership to strengthen philanthropic support and advance strategic fundraising initiatives.

This individual will lead donor identification, cultivation, solicitation, stewardship, and pipeline development efforts while building meaningful relationships with alumni, donors, corporations, foundations, and community partners. The Senior Director will also collaborate across the university to align donor interests with institutional priorities and advance a culture of philanthropy across major, principal, and planned giving.

With a new university president, new college leadership, and a future comprehensive campaign on the horizon, this role offers the opportunity to help shape the next chapter of philanthropy for one of the university’s largest colleges.

Major & Principal Gift Fundraising
Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major gifts of $25,000+ with a focus on gifts above $100,000, including principal gifts at the $1 million+ level from individuals, corporations, and foundations.
Develop strategic cultivation and solicitation plans aligned with college and university priorities.
Manage the full donor lifecycle, including prospect identification, relationship management, stewardship, and ongoing engagement.
Prepare donor-facing materials including proposals, gift agreements, and stewardship communications.

University-Wide Collaboration & Corporate Partnerships
Partner with university leadership, faculty, and advancement colleagues to identify philanthropic priorities and strategic fundraising opportunities.
Manage and coordinate relationships with corporate and foundation partners supporting multiple colleges and university initiatives.
Collaborate with fellow directors of development on interdisciplinary fundraising efforts and university-wide initiatives.

Volunteer & Donor Engagement
Develop and support strategic volunteer engagement opportunities for major gift prospects and donors.
Enlist, train, and partner with volunteers and advisory boards in support of fundraising initiatives and donor engagement strategies.
Represent CHHS and the university at events and donor engagement activities as needed.

Strategic Planning & Development Leadership
Partner with URD leadership and the dean of CHHS to identify fundraising priorities and develop strategic advancement plans.
Provide guidance and support related to fundraising strategy, donor engagement, and philanthropic opportunities.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree required.

Demonstrated success securing major gifts and building donor relationships.
Experience in higher education or similarly complex fundraising environments preferred.

jobs.description:
About Us

Brilla Schools, a growing K-8 network in the Bronx, serves over 2,000 students with plans to expand to educate 3,000 across four elementary and four middle schools. Managed by Seton Education Partners, Brilla Schools are dedicated to forming students of strong wisdom and virtue. Our classically inspired approach to education combines a content-rich curriculum, inquiry-driven learning, and a focus on virtues, while providing individualized support to meet each child's unique needs. A national leader in character education and supporting students with varying needs, over the past two years, Brilla alumni have secured spots in the most prestigious high schools in the tri-state area, earning over $3 million in scholarships and financial aid. Our staff are mission-aligned change-makers who believe in fostering a joyful, rigorous learning environment, and Brilla offers some of the most competitive salaries in the market to honor their dedication. With high expectations and a supportive community, we're preparing students to excel in high school, college, and beyond.

Position Overview

Brilla Schools seeks a mission-driven, results-oriented leader to serve as Managing Director of Enrollment for the Brilla Schools Network in the Bronx. The Managing Director of Enrollment will own and execute the network-wide recruitment, enrollment and retention strategy across elementary and middle school portfolios, ensuring Brilla meets ambitious growth, retention, and compliance goals while delivering an exceptional, family-centered enrollment experience.

This role is ideal for a strategic, data-driven leader with deep marketing and enrollment operations experience who can both set vision and build durable systems, while coaching and developing a high-performing team. The Managing Director of Enrollment reports to the Chief of Staff and partners closely with school leaders, operations, data, marketing, and external vendors

This role owns a department or function across the network, including strategy, systems, and performance outcomes. The Managing Director of Enrollment designs and implements processes that drive quality, equity, and consistency, manages Managers and/or team leads, and uses data and stakeholder feedback to improve results. This leader ensures strong execution while building sustainable systems for growth.

The Managing Director of Enrollment provides strategic leadership, systems ownership, and people management for all enrollment and retention efforts across the Brilla Schools Network. This role ensures enrollment operations are compliant, efficient, data-informed, and family-centered, while driving consistent practices and strong results across campuses.

Core Competencies & Responsibilities

Enrollment Strategy & Network Oversight

Own and execute the network-wide recruitment and enrollment strategy across elementary and middle school portfolios.
Set annual and quarterly recruitment and enrollment goals in partnership with senior leadership.
Analyze full-funnel enrollment data including leads, applications, offers, yield, retention, attrition, discharges, and no-shows to forecast trends and proactively mitigate risk.
Monitor and manage the full enrollment funnel, ensuring strong follow-up, lead nurturing, and conversion practices.
Regularly evaluate enrollment initiatives and sunset low-impact strategies in favor of high-yield practices.

Enrollment Team Leadership & People Management

Serve as people manager for the network-wide enrollment team, including Enrollment Managers, Student Recruiter Coordinators, and dotted line manager of Enrollment Captains.
Set clear roles, expectations, performance metrics, and accountability structures.
Lead regular 1:1s, coaching sessions, and performance check-ins.
Identify skill gaps and coordinate onboarding, professional development, and training.
Foster a collaborative, mission-driven team culture aligned to Brilla norms and goals.
Make staffing recommendations, including role design, hiring needs, and organizational improvements.
Ensure appropriate coverage, workload balance, and clear escalation pathways across campuses.

Systems Ownership & Data Integrity

Serve as system owner for SchoolMint, HubSpot, ATS, PowerSchool, and all enrollment-related workflows.
Ensure systems are accurate, aligned, and efficient across platforms.
Oversee network-wide data hygiene, cleanup, deduplication, and integrity efforts.
Partner with Data and Operations teams to resolve system issues and streamline processes.
Leverage data to drive forecasting, decision-making, and leadership reporting.

Lottery & Compliance Management

Lead and oversee the annual enrollment lottery in full compliance with authorizer and state requirements.
Ensure correct prioritization, offer management, documentation, and communication timelines.
Maintain accountability for lottery setup, execution, and system readiness.
Train enrollment staff on lottery procedures and compliance expectations.

Retention Strategy & Oversight

Own and manage network-wide student retention strategies in partnership with campus leadership and enrollment captains.
Analyze attrition and discharge trends and identify root causes.
Develop and adjust campus-specific retention plans to minimize withdrawals.
Partner with school leaders to implement timely interventions for at-risk families.
Track retention metrics and integrate insights into seat planning and projections.

Enrollment Events & Campus-Based Recruitment

Design, standardize, and oversee high-impact enrollment events, including ACE events and New to Brilla events.
Establish clear goals, timelines, staffing plans, and success metrics.
Ensure events are family-centered, well-executed, and aligned to network priorities.
Evaluate outcomes and continuously refine event models to maximize conversion.

Family Engagement & Community Growth

Ensure enrollment practices are timely, equitable, and family-centered.
Oversee enrollment communications, outreach standards, and follow-up practices.
Guide open houses, tours, community-based recruitment, and neighborhood outreach.
Oversee Family Ambassador programs, Partner Parish outreach, and CBO partnerships.
Identify and remove systemic barriers to enrollment and retention.

Consultant & Vendor Management

Manage external recruitment, CRM, and enrollment and marketing consultants.
Serve as primary point of contact for HubSpot optimization consultants, translating enrollment needs into workflows and reporting.
Set scopes of work, timelines, deliverables, and success metrics.
Evaluate consultant effectiveness and ROI.

External Partnerships & Marketing Channels

Engage with external partners (billboards, subway, out-of-home advertising).
Identify and evaluate new marketing channels based on cost, reach, and yield.
Coordinate with marketing and operations teams to ensure alignment with brand and timelines.
Track campaign performance and make data-informed recommendations.

SOP Development & Operational Excellence

Own and approve Standard Operating Procedures for all enrollment processes (applications, lottery, transfers, discharges, withdrawals).
Ensure SOPs are documented, trained, and consistently implemented.
Identify inefficiencies and lead continuous improvement efforts.
Partner cross-functionally to strengthen workflows and execution.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Reporting

Serve as the primary enrollment liaison to senior leadership.
Provide regular enrollment updates, projections, and risk assessments.
Partner with campus leaders to align enrollment strategy with school culture and capacity.
Support leadership decision-making with clear, actionable insights.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required
5+ years of enrollment, operations, or school-based leadership experience
Experience managing teams and coaching staff
Strong proficiency in Google Suite, Excel, and data systems
Experience with SchoolMint, PowerSchool, ATS, HubSpot, or similar platforms strongly preferred
Fluency in Spanish is a plus
Demonstrated ability to quickly build productive and meaningful relationships with multiple stakeholders including school and network based staff, families, and community members
Proven ability to effectively support, collaborate, and partner with a variety of personalities and working styles and an openness and generosity of spirit in navigating differences
A strong capacity to coach and develop others, providing guidance and support to ensure operational excellence and compliance across the network
Project management expertise and the ability to drive efficiency and excellence in all aspects of work alongside and/or through others
Optimistic self-starter with the ability to prioritize competing goals, exhibit flexibility, grace and sound judgment along with productive urgency in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment
Ability to leverage data to drive operational decisions, identify trends, and implement strategic improvements to enhance overall effectiveness and compliance across the network.
Strong strategic thinking, analytical and creative problem-solving skills
Flexible and willing to perform other duties as assigned
Ability to travel approximately 10-20% of the time, primarily within the US

Benefits

At Brilla Schools, we celebrate the unique skills, experiences, and passions that each staff member brings to our mission. To support their work, we offer a thoughtfully designed benefits package to provide competitive and adaptable coverage. We are committed to offering a benefits portfolio that supports the holistic health and wellness of our team members including:

: More than 225 hours annually, featuring two weeks of onboarding, coaching, and targeted training sessions to ensure staff excel in their roles and flourish.

Community and Culture

At Brilla, your dedication fuels our mission, and we're here to invest in your growth, well-being, and success—from recruitment to retirement!

Email resume and cover letter to Sara Jones, Co-Chair Executive Director Search Committee, at sara@friendsforsight.org

About Friends for Sight

Through vision screenings, comprehensive eye exams, prescription glasses, mobile clinics, and community partnerships, Friends for Sight ensures that every Utahn, regardless of income or background, has access to quality vision care.

Our Vision:
A future where every Utahn has access to the vision care they need to learn, work, and thrive.

Position Summary

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of Friends for Sight and is responsible for advancing the organization's mission through strategic leadership, financial stewardship, fundraising, organizational management, and community engagement. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director leads the organization's staff, cultivates strong partnerships, and ensures Friends for Sight remains financially sustainable while expanding its impact across Utah.

The Executive Director works collaboratively with the Operations Manager, Development Director, as part of a small staff of 8-10 employees and a broad network of hundreds of volunteers to implement the Board's strategic vision, strengthen organizational capacity, and build meaningful relationships with donors, community partners, and policymakers.

●      Support grant development, stewardship, and donor engagement.
●      Participate in fundraising campaigns, special events, and donor cultivation activities.
●      Strengthen long-term philanthropic investment in Friends for Sight.

Board Relations

●      Serve as the primary liaison between the Board of Directors and staff.
●      Support Board recruitment, orientation, engagement, and governance.
●      Prepare Board meeting materials, strategic recommendations, and organizational reports.
●      Partner with Board committees to accomplish organizational priorities.
●      Ensure compliance with Board policies and nonprofit governance best practices.

Community Partnerships & External Relations

●      Serve as the primary public representative and spokesperson for Friends for Sight.
●      Develop and strengthen strategic partnerships with healthcare providers, school districts, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and community leaders.
●      Represent Friends for Sight at community events, conferences, legislative meetings, and public forums.
●      Advocate for vision screening and accessible vision care throughout Utah.
●      Increase the organization's visibility, influence, and reputation statewide.

Organizational Leadership

●      Recruit, supervise, mentor, and develop high-performing staff.
●      Cultivate a workplace culture where every employee, volunteer, Board member, partner, and community member is treated with dignity, respect, and fairness, establishing these principles as the standard for all organizational relationships.
●      Align staff with organizational priorities while fostering collaboration, accountability, transparency, and professional growth.
●      Promote effective communication and shared leadership across the organization.

Financial Stewardship

●      Partner with accounting staff and the Board Treasurer to develop and oversee the annual operating and program budgets.
●      Ensure sound financial management, internal controls, and responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
●      Monitor financial performance and recommend adjustments to support long-term sustainability.
●      Oversee investment and cash management strategies in collaboration with the Finance Committee.
●      Ensure compliance with nonprofit accounting standards, grant agreements, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements.
●      Present accurate and timely financial information to the Board of Directors.

Program & Operations Leadership

●      Provide strategic leadership and support to the Operations Manager to ensure programs and operations advance the organization's mission and strategic priorities.
●      Ensure organizational resources, staffing, and systems support effective program delivery and long-term sustainability.
●      Review organizational performance and use program data to inform strategic decisions and continuous improvement.
●      Encourage innovation and organizational learning to strengthen services and expand community impact.

Operations & Compliance

●      Oversee organizational policies, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
●      Ensure compliance with HIPAA, employment law, nonprofit regulations, and organizational policies.
●      Oversee organizational technology, facilities, insurance, and key vendor relationships.
●      Ensure operational systems support organizational effectiveness and long-term sustainability.

Qualifications

Required

●      Bachelor’s degree
●      Minimum of five years of progressively responsible leadership experience.
●      Demonstrated success supervising staff and leading organizational operations.
●      Experience leading organizational growth, strategic planning, and change management.
●      Experience developing and managing organizational budgets.
●      Proven success developing and executing fundraising strategies, cultivating and stewarding donors, supporting grants, and/or building long-term philanthropic and community relationships.
●      Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with demonstrated experience representing an organization publicly and building community visibility.
●      Ability to build collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders.

Valued, but not required.

●      Familiarity with Utah’s nonprofit, philanthropic, healthcare, or community landscape, including relationships relevant to fundraising, strategic partnerships, and statewide service delivery. Comparable experience in another market and a demonstrated ability to quickly develop local knowledge and build trusted relationships will also be considered.
●      Advanced degree or equivalent professional experience demonstrating the capabilities needed for the role.
●      Executive Director or senior nonprofit leadership experience.

Friends for Sight offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including:

●      Paid time off and paid holidays
●      SIMPLE IRA retirement plan with a 3% employer match (fully vested on day 1)
●      Professional development, leadership coaching, and continuing education
●      A flexible, family-friendly hybrid work environment that supports work-life balance

Person-Centered Care

We treat everyone with dignity and respect, valuing each person’s unique needs and experiences.

Mission-Driven Integrity

We are unwavering in our commitment to our mission, making thoughtful, strategic decisions that maximize impact

Community Partnership

We believe lasting impact comes from collaboration—working alongside communities to expand access to quality vision care.

Excellence in Vision Care

We are committed to staying current with vision care best practices, ensuring the delivery of high-quality, accessible services that meet the evolving needs of the communities we serve.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity
﻿
The Family Peace Center of Washington County is seeking an exceptional Executive Director to lead the organization through its next stage of growth, sustainability, and impact.

The Family Peace Center brings more than 20 organizations together in one collaborative environment to create a more coordinated response for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and child abuse. Community-based organizations, law enforcement, prosecution, medical providers, and family support services work alongside one another so survivors and families do not have to navigate complex and fragmented systems alone.

The next Executive Director will join an organization that has undergone significant transformation and is ready to build for the future.

This leader will strengthen the organization's foundation, advance financial sustainability, deepen community and philanthropic relationships, develop the team and operating infrastructure, and align partners around a shared vision for coordinated, survivor-centered care.

This is an opportunity for a leader who is energized not simply by running an organization, but by building what comes next.

The Role

The Executive Director serves as the Family Peace Center's chief executive, organizational leader, fundraiser, community ambassador, and strategic partner to the Board of Directors.

The role requires someone who can move comfortably between strategy and execution, relationships and accountability, organizational leadership and systems change.

The Executive Director will:
Set a clear strategic direction and translate it into measurable priorities and results.
Build the organizational infrastructure, systems, and accountability needed for long-term success.
Lead, develop, and support a strong team.
Strengthen collaboration across an ecosystem of 20+ partner organizations.
Build trusted relationships with community leaders, government partners, funders, donors, and other stakeholders.
Lead fundraising and revenue strategy, including major donor and institutional relationships.
Diversify revenue and strengthen long-term financial sustainability.
Provide strong financial and operational stewardship.
Partner effectively with the Board on strategy, governance, fundraising, and organizational accountability.
Represent the Family Peace Center as a credible and compelling voice for collaborative, survivor-centered systems change.

What Success Looks Like

The next Executive Director will lead the Family Peace Center from a period of significant growth and transformation into its next chapter of organizational strength, financial sustainability, and community impact.

Success will mean:
A strong, sustainable organization: Clear priorities, disciplined operations, strong leadership, and the systems and accountability needed for long-term success.
A thriving partnership ecosystem: Strong relationships and alignment across partner organizations, public systems, funders, community stakeholders, and the Board—with shared priorities and collective ownership of outcomes.
A stronger community-wide response: A coordinated, survivor-centered system that reduces barriers and improves access to safety, healing, and support for survivors and families.
A diversified, sustainable financial model: Strong philanthropic relationships, expanded revenue sources, increased fundraising capacity, and greater long-term financial stability.

Fundraising and financial sustainability will be significant measures of success. The Executive Director will be directly accountable for growing philanthropic support, diversifying revenue, and building lasting donor relationships.

The Leader We're Looking For

We are looking for an executive leader, relationship builder, and systems thinker who can turn vision into action and bring people together around a shared purpose.

You may be a strong fit if you:
Think strategically and translate vision into clear priorities, action, and results.
Build trust and alignment across organizations, systems, and competing perspectives.
Lead through influence and relationships as effectively as through formal authority.
Balance empathy and emotional intelligence with clarity, accountability, and sound judgment.
Move comfortably between Board leadership, fundraising, community partnerships, and internal operations.
Thrive in a lean environment and are willing to step into the work when needed.
Bring people together around shared goals while navigating complexity and change.
Believe lasting impact is built through collaboration, shared ownership, and strong relationships.

Above all, we are looking for a leader who brings humility, authenticity, courage, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to shared success.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a relevant field; master's degree preferred.
At least five years of executive or senior leadership experience, including responsibility for leading people, organizations, programs, or complex initiatives.
Demonstrated success in fundraising, donor engagement, and/or revenue development.
Grant writing and/or grant management experience.
Experience partnering effectively with a governing Board.
Strong financial, operational, and organizational judgment.
Demonstrated success leading in complex, resource-conscious environments.
Exceptional communication, facilitation, diplomacy, and relationship-building skills.
Proven ability to navigate multiple stakeholders, build consensus, and move shared priorities forward.

Experience That Will Set You Apart

We are especially interested in candidates who bring experience in one or more of the following:
Nonprofit executive or senior leadership.
Public, community, or human-services systems.
Multi-agency partnerships or collaborative service models.
Philanthropy, major gifts, fundraising, or donor development.
Domestic violence, sexual assault, child abuse, victim services, or related systems of care.
Washington County or the broader regional philanthropic, government, and community landscape.

There is no single path to this role. We welcome leaders from different backgrounds whose experience demonstrates the judgment, capabilities, and commitment needed to lead the Family Peace Center into its next chapter.

Why the Family Peace Center

This is an opportunity to lead more than an organization. It is an opportunity to help strengthen a community-wide system of care.

The next Executive Director will build on a transformational model, strengthen its long-term sustainability, deepen collaboration across organizations and systems, and help shape how Washington County responds to violence, trauma, healing, and hope.

If you are energized by building strong organizations, developing sustainable resources, navigating complex systems, and bringing people together around work that matters, we would welcome the opportunity to learn more about you.

About the Family Peace Center

The Family Peace Center of Washington County is a collaborative, multi-agency center providing a single location for prevention, intervention, healing, and hope for survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, and child abuse.

More than 20 partner organizations—including community-based organizations, law enforcement, prosecution, medical providers, and family support services—work within an integrated ecosystem designed to improve safety, access, coordination, and long-term outcomes.

The Family Peace Center is both a service hub and a systems-change initiative, bringing partners together around shared responsibility for creating a more coordinated, trauma-informed, and survivor-centered community response.

Location & Work Expectations

This position is based at the Family Peace Center of Washington County in Hillsboro, Oregon. The Executive Director is expected to maintain a meaningful on-site presence given the highly collaborative nature of the role and the importance of relationships with staff, partners, community stakeholders, and funders.

The role includes local and regional travel and occasional evening or weekend commitments related to Board meetings, community engagement, fundraising, and organizational events.

Compensation & Benefits

The hiring range for this position is $115,000–$135,000 annually. Starting salary will be determined based on the selected candidate's relevant experience, qualifications, demonstrated capabilities, and alignment with the requirements of the position.

The Family Peace Center offers a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, and vision insurance with a competitive employer contribution; life insurance; and an employer-sponsored retirement plan with matching contribution.

Esteemed is seeking a growth operator to co-found and lead Esteemed Cloud, the AI builder and cloud platform operated within the Esteemed holding company. Esteemed is a small, revenue-first permanent holding company building AI-native platforms for work. No exit is required; liquidity comes through distributions and buyouts. Each operating company licenses a shared technology group and AI substrate (Esteemed Intelligence) from the parent; none manages its own engineering. Esteemed's products include HCMGPT (the AI Operator for HR, Staffing, and PeopleOps), Esteemed Acquire and Hire (CRM and ATS), the Colleagues network, and Esteemed Cloud. Chris McGrath, Founder & CEO, Esteemed — 25+ years building talent and web platforms; former AT&T (Hypergrowth) and Accenture Digital
Tom Schmidt, Co-founder & CSO, Esteemed — 30 years in staffing; former SVP Recruit Holdings (Indeed, Glassdoor, Staffmark), former VP ManpowerGroup
Rick Savage, Strategic Advisor — former Head of Talent Acquisition, Workday; leads Global Recruiting Operations Technology at NVIDIA

Esteemed Cloud (https://esteemed.io) is a combination AI Website / App builder and cloud platform. Create, the builder, was engineered for head-to-head competition with Lovable and Replit while also making it easy to incorporate AI into your app: describe an app or site in plain language, get working software, edit by conversation, publish to Esteemed Cloud. The platform has run enterprise hosting operations for six years, with delivery history spanning major non-profits, state and federal governments, and universities.

What makes the current iteration unique is the bundle. Lovable deploys to someone else's hosting. Base44 had no domains, no expert bench, and few enterprise customers when Wix paid ~$80M for it — precisely to bolt a builder onto hosting, domains, and an SMB base. Esteemed already is that combination: a Replit- and Lovable-level builder with native cloud hosting underneath it, domains, and more — similar to Odoo — we offer a family of business apps (CRM, ATS, CMS, commerce, intelligence) that install behind whatever the customer builds. Plus the piece nobody in the category has natively: Hire an Expert, a 35,000-professional vetted network attached to the product built over years. So the customer who outgrows the AI or burns their credits half-finished can convert to a human engagement instead of churning in frustration. Competitors monetize the build. Esteemed Cloud monetizes build, run, and grow — builder usage, hosting MRR, domains, Managed support, app upsell, and expert placements from the same account. Esteemed Intelligence runs underneath, so generation quality and recommendations improve with use.

Create — (live) builder subscriptions plus metered token usage
Self-serve Cloud — (live) hosting, domains; premium-domain reseller line in negotiation
Managed hosting — (live, unmarketed) done-for-you tier with the free AI-rebuild close designed; modest existing revenue

Acquisition engine — (separate ledger) hosting/MSP books acquired via holdco-led financing land on Cloud's ARR in addition to the organic mandate

A live product, a built funnel, six years of hosting operations, and enterprise delivery history

About SF New Deal:

SF New Deal (SFND) is a 501(c)3 nonprofit that provides supportive services and financial opportunities for small businesses in San Francisco. Our mission is to strengthen neighborhoods by making it easier for under-resourced small business owners to succeed. We envision and are building towards a vibrant San Francisco with diverse and thriving small businesses.

Our team is growing rapidly to build and deliver innovative and responsive community-centered solutions to some of San Francisco’s most persistent challenges. Since our launch in March 2020, we’ve had significant impact and disbursed over $60 million dollars to over 2000 small businesses citywide through a host of diverse programs. Our work is funded through private donations and government contracts.

We’re a team of collaborative optimists and would love to have you join and build with us.

About the role:

SF New Deal seeks a strategic, collaborative, and execution-oriented Deputy Director of Small Business Systems & Navigation to lead the coordination of the small-business support ecosystem in San Francisco.

San Francisco has a substantial network of public agencies, nonprofit organizations, lenders, funders, technical-assistance providers, and neighborhood-based initiatives serving small businesses. Yet entrepreneurs are often required to navigate multiple applications, overlapping eligibility requirements, and informal referral processes to find the support that meets their needs.

The Deputy Director will lead SF New Deal’s No Wrong Door initiative, a multi-year effort to create a clearer and more coordinated entry point for small-business assistance. The initiative will establish shared referral infrastructure, strengthen coordination among providers, and develop technology that helps businesses identify and access appropriate capital, technical assistance, and other resources.
This is a senior leadership role for someone who can work across strategy, partnerships, program operations, technology, and data. The Deputy Director will serve as the principal architect and accountable driver for the initiative, moving it from stakeholder alignment and prototyping through public launch, adoption, and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategy, Systems Design, and Implementation
Define and manage the strategy, operating model, implementation plan, budget, and performance measures for the No Wrong Door initiative.
Design a coordinated intake, assessment, referral, and follow-up system that makes it easier for small businesses to access appropriate capital, technical assistance, and other resources.
Lead the initiative from provider mapping and prototyping through launch, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Oversee the development of accessible, secure, and practical technology supporting intake, eligibility assessment, referrals, and provider coordination.
Manage staff, consultants, vendors, and cross-functional workstreams to deliver the initiative on time and within budget.

Partnerships, Provider Coordination, and Adoption
Build and manage a network of government agencies, community organizations, lenders, funders, technical-assistance providers, and neighborhood partners.
Establish shared referral protocols, service expectations, eligibility information, data-sharing practices, and mechanisms for resolving unsuccessful referrals.
Convene partners to identify service gaps, reduce duplication, and improve coordination across the small-business support ecosystem.
Lead provider onboarding, training, communications, and adoption of the intake and referral system.
Represent SF New Deal with senior external stakeholders, funders, public agencies, and community partners.

Operations, Data, and Continuous Improvement
Oversee the day-to-day operation and quality of the navigation and referral system, including referral integrity, responsiveness, and user experience.
Establish measures for access, referral completion, response time, service utilization, capital connection, equity, and business-owner satisfaction.
Use quantitative data and stakeholder feedback to identify gaps, improve workflows, and inform recommendations to providers, funders, and public agencies.
Produce regular reports for organizational leadership, funders, and participating partners.
Ensure the initiative remains responsive to changing business needs, provider capacity, eligibility requirements, and funding conditions.

Key Proficiencies:

Visionary strategic thinking with a proven ability to design and lead programs that anticipate future needs and opportunities for small businesses.
Strong partnership skills, with the ability to collaborate closely with peers, direct reports and senior leadership, to bring program ideas to life and refine them as needed.
Ability to synthesize complex data and feedback from multiple sources into actionable program strategies that drive impact.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to inspire and motivate both internal teams and external stakeholders around a shared vision for the future.
Experience with program evaluation and a data-driven approach to assessing program effectiveness and impact.
Creative problem-solving abilities, with a focus on continuous improvement and innovation in program design.
Strong understanding of the challenges and opportunities facing small businesses, particularly in under-resourced communities.

Qualifications
At least five years of experience in economic development, small-business support, public-sector innovation, nonprofit leadership, community development, financial inclusion, program design, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through implementation.
Strong knowledge of the needs and operating realities of small businesses, particularly businesses owned by historically underserved entrepreneurs.
Track record of building alignment among government agencies, nonprofit organizations, financial institutions, funders, and community partners.
Experience designing or improving intake, referral, navigation, case-management, or service-delivery systems.
Experience managing technology-enabled projects, digital products, databases, customer-relationship-management systems, or similar platforms.
Strong project and people management skills, including experience managing staff, consultants, vendors, budgets, and multiple concurrent workstreams.
Ability to define performance measures, interpret quantitative and qualitative data, and use findings to improve programs and influence strategy.
Excellent facilitation, negotiation, writing, presentation, and relationship-management skills.
Ability to move comfortably between high-level strategy and detailed execution in a fast-changing environment.
Sound judgment, strong follow-through, and a collaborative leadership style.
Commitment to equitable access, user-centered design, and reducing administrative burdens for small-business owners.
Bachelor’s degree in public policy, public administration, business administration, economics, urban planning, information systems, data analytics, community development, or a closely related field; advanced degree preferred.
Experience working in the San Francisco small-business, economic-development, or community-development ecosystem.
Familiarity with small-business lending, grants, technical assistance, commercial leasing, permitting, procurement, or neighborhood economic development.
Experience launching a new program, collaborative network, or technology-enabled service.

How to Apply

Email resume and cover letter to Sara Jones, Co-Chair Executive Director Search Committee, at sara@friendsforsight.org

About Friends for Sight

Friends for Sight believes accessible vision care opens the door to discovery—creating a ripple effect for generations. Through vision screenings, comprehensive eye exams, prescription glasses, mobile clinics, and community partnerships, Friends for Sight ensures that every Utahn, regardless of income or background, has access to quality vision care.

Our Vision:
A future where every Utahn has access to the vision care they need to learn, work, and thrive.

Position Summary

The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of Friends for Sight and is responsible for advancing the organization's mission through strategic leadership, financial stewardship, fundraising, organizational management, and community engagement. Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director leads the organization's staff, cultivates strong partnerships, and ensures Friends for Sight remains financially sustainable while expanding its impact across Utah.

The Executive Director works collaboratively with the Operations Manager, Development Director, as part of a small staff of 8-10 employees and a broad network of hundreds of volunteers to implement the Board's strategic vision, strengthen organizational capacity, and build meaningful relationships with donors, community partners, and policymakers.

Essential Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

●      Monitor organizational performance, identify emerging opportunities and challenges, and recommend strategic adjustments as needed.

●      Cultivate relationships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, and government partners.
●      Identify and pursue new funding opportunities.
●      Support grant development, stewardship, and donor engagement.
●      Participate in fundraising campaigns, special events, and donor cultivation activities.
●      Strengthen long-term philanthropic investment in Friends for Sight.

Board Relations

●      Serve as the primary liaison between the Board of Directors and staff.
●      Support Board recruitment, orientation, engagement, and governance.
●      Prepare Board meeting materials, strategic recommendations, and organizational reports.
●      Partner with Board committees to accomplish organizational priorities.
●      Ensure compliance with Board policies and nonprofit governance best practices.

Community Partnerships & External Relations

●      Serve as the primary public representative and spokesperson for Friends for Sight.
●      Develop and strengthen strategic partnerships with healthcare providers, school districts, government agencies, nonprofit organizations, and community leaders.
●      Represent Friends for Sight at community events, conferences, legislative meetings, and public forums.
●      Advocate for vision screening and accessible vision care throughout Utah.
●      Increase the organization's visibility, influence, and reputation statewide.

Organizational Leadership

●      Recruit, supervise, mentor, and develop high-performing staff.
●      Cultivate a workplace culture where every employee, volunteer, Board member, partner, and community member is treated with dignity, respect, and fairness, establishing these principles as the standard for all organizational relationships.
●      Align staff with organizational priorities while fostering collaboration, accountability, transparency, and professional growth.
●      Promote effective communication and shared leadership across the organization.

Financial Stewardship

●      Partner with accounting staff and the Board Treasurer to develop and oversee the annual operating and program budgets.
●      Ensure sound financial management, internal controls, and responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
●      Monitor financial performance and recommend adjustments to support long-term sustainability.
●      Oversee investment and cash management strategies in collaboration with the Finance Committee.
●      Ensure compliance with nonprofit accounting standards, grant agreements, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements.
●      Present accurate and timely financial information to the Board of Directors.

●      Provide strategic leadership and support to the Operations Manager to ensure programs and operations advance the organization's mission and strategic priorities.
●      Ensure organizational resources, staffing, and systems support effective program delivery and long-term sustainability.
●      Review organizational performance and use program data to inform strategic decisions and continuous improvement.
●      Encourage innovation and organizational learning to strengthen services and expand community impact.

Operations & Compliance

●      Oversee organizational policies, risk management, and regulatory compliance.
●      Ensure compliance with HIPAA, employment law, nonprofit regulations, and organizational policies.
●      Oversee organizational technology, facilities, insurance, and key vendor relationships.
●      Ensure operational systems support organizational effectiveness and long-term sustainability.

Qualifications

Required

●      Bachelor’s degree
●      Minimum of five years of progressively responsible leadership experience.
●      Demonstrated success supervising staff and leading organizational operations.
●      Experience leading organizational growth, strategic planning, and change management.
●      Experience developing and managing organizational budgets.
●      Proven success developing and executing fundraising strategies, cultivating and stewarding donors, supporting grants, and/or building long-term philanthropic and community relationships.
●      Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with demonstrated experience representing an organization publicly and building community visibility.
●      Ability to build collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders.

Valued, but not required.

●      Familiarity with Utah’s nonprofit, philanthropic, healthcare, or community landscape, including relationships relevant to fundraising, strategic partnerships, and statewide service delivery. Comparable experience in another market and a demonstrated ability to quickly develop local knowledge and build trusted relationships will also be considered.
●      Advanced degree or equivalent professional experience demonstrating the capabilities needed for the role.
●      Executive Director or senior nonprofit leadership experience.
●      Experience working closely with nonprofit Boards of Directors.

Compensation & Benefits

Friends for Sight offers a competitive compensation and benefits package, including:

●      Professional development, leadership coaching, and continuing education

Our Values

At Friends for Sight, we are guided by five core values:

We treat everyone with dignity and respect, valuing each person’s unique needs and experiences.

We are unwavering in our commitment to our mission, making thoughtful, strategic decisions that maximize impact
